newsitem.title: JAPAN: Pace of decline in Japan trade surplus slowing-MOF.
newsitem.headline: Pace of decline in Japan trade surplus slowing-MOF.

text.p: The pace of the decline in Japan's trade surplus is slowing, Vice Finance Minster Tadashi Ogawa told reporters on Monday.
Ogawa said the pace of the increase in imports to Japan had continued to slow while exports had risen more than 10 percent each month on a year-on-year basis for the last several months.
"It is true that the tempo of the decline in the trade surplus has slowed down," he said.
Data released on Monday by the Finance Ministry showed Japan's overall customs-cleared trade surplus grew 163.7 percent to 831.48 billion yen in April.
But Ogawa said it would be necessary to monitor future movements for a while before making a judgment on the outlook for the trade account.
He also said the April figures were affected by the rise in Japan's consumption tax on April 1 to five percent from three percent.
Ogawa also said it would be difficult to judge when the effects of the recent strengthening of the yen would appear in the trade data.
"There is a time lag between the strengthening or the weakening of the yen and its effect on the trade account," he said.
Ogawa reiterated that Tokyo has told U.S. authorities that there will be no substantial rise in its trade surplus in the medium to longer term. -- Tokyo Policy Desk +81-3-5473-3710
